content.name: p
children: TNTSearch supports dynamic index updates, allowing you to insert new documents, update existing ones, and delete documents without rebuilding the entire index. This is essential for keeping your search index in sync with your application data.

content.name: p
children: Add new documents to an existing index:

content.name: Fence
p
children: The array keys must match the columns used when the index was created. After insertion, the document is immediately searchable:

content.name: Fence
children:
$results = $tnt->search('Othello');
// [13]

content.name: h2
children: Updating documents

content.name: p
children: Update an existing document by providing its ID and the new content:

content.name: Fence
p
children: The update process removes the old document data from the index and inserts the new data. Word counts and document frequencies are adjusted automatically.

content.name: p
children: If the document ID doesn't exist in the index,

children.name: code
children: update()
acts as an insert and the total document count increases.

content.name: h2
children: Deleting documents

content.name: p
children: Remove a document from the index by its ID:

content.name: Fence
children: $index->delete(12);

content.name: p
children: After deletion, the document will no longer appear in search results. Word counts and document frequencies are decremented accordingly.

content.name: h2
children: Monitoring index state

content.name: p
children: You can check the total number of indexed documents:

content.name: Fence
children:
$total = $tnt->totalDocumentsInCollection();
echo "Total documents: $total"; // e.g., 12

content.name: p
children: This count updates automatically as you insert and delete documents.

children: For applications with frequent data changes, consider running index updates in a queue or background job to avoid slowing down your main application flow.
